tools.name: CreateExperiment
tools.description:
Create an A/B test experiment as a draft, with its feature flag.

The flag stays off and nobody is enrolled until the experiment is
launched. Before creating, verify the feature_flag_key is not
already used by another experiment and that the metrics' event
names exist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Experiment name describing the hypothesis.

parameters.name: feature_flag_key
parameters.description: Key of the experiment's feature flag. Lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores only. When no flag has this key, PostHog creates one; when a flag already has it, the experiment uses that flag as it is, and variants and rollout_percentage must be omitted.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: PostHog project ID.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Detailed hypothesis and expected outcome. Defaults to no description.

parameters.name: experiment_type
parameters.description: Experiment type. Defaults to PostHog's default type.

parameters.name: primary_metrics
parameters.description: Judge the experiment by these metrics. Defaults to no primary metrics.

parameters.name: secondary_metrics
parameters.description: Also track these metrics to watch for side effects. Defaults to no secondary metrics.

parameters.name: variants
parameters.description: Split users between these variants. Their rollout percentages must add up to 100. Defaults to a 50/50 split between control and test.

parameters.name: rollout_percentage
parameters.description: Enroll this percentage of users (0-100) in the experiment. Defaults to 100.

parameters.description: The HogQL SELECT query to run. HogQL is PostHog's SQL dialect over tables such as events, persons, and sessions; filter events by timestamp to keep the scan small. Without a LIMIT clause, PostHog returns at most 100 rows; page further with LIMIT and OFFSET.

summary:
## PostHog Toolkit for Arcade

Enables LLM-powered interaction with [PostHog](https://posthog.com) analytics — querying events, managing feature flags, experiments, surveys, dashboards, insights, and error tracking via the PostHog API.

## Capabilities

- **Event & data exploration:** List event definitions and properties, run HogQL queries, fetch time-series trends, funnels, and cohort retention data, and compare metrics across date ranges.
- **Dashboards & insights:** Create, read, update, and delete dashboards; create, pin, update, and soft-delete saved insights.
- **Feature flags:** Create, read, update, and soft-delete flags; control rollout rules and targeting; validate key uniqueness before creation.
- **A/B experiments:** Create draft experiments with linked feature flags, launch and archive them, retrieve per-variant statistical results (chance to win, credible intervals, exposures).
- **Surveys:** Create, read, update, archive, and list surveys; review activity logs of survey changes.
- **Error tracking:** List and retrieve error issues with status, severity, and assignee detail.

## Secrets

This toolkit requires two secrets. Set them via the [Arcade secrets dashboard](https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets) or through the API.

- **`POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY`** — A PostHog Personal API Key used to authenticate all API requests. Generate one in your PostHog account under **Settings → Personal API keys** (top-right user menu → *Your profile → Personal API keys*). The key must have access to the project(s) you intend to query. See [PostHog docs on personal API keys](https://posthog.com/docs/api#private-endpoint-authentication) for details on creating and scoping them.

- **`POSTHOG_SERVER_URL`** — The base URL of your PostHog instance. For PostHog Cloud US this is `https://us.posthog.com`; for EU Cloud it is `https://eu.posthog.com`; for self-hosted deployments, use your own domain (e.g., `https://posthog.example.com`). This tells the toolkit which instance to route requests to.

For general guidance on configuring secrets in Arcade, see the [Arcade secrets documentation](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets).
